analysis.headline: Marina kills Chuy González Peñuelas, Cártel de Guasave figure wanted by the US, in northern Sinaloa
analysis.what_happened: Navy forces killed Jesús González Peñuelas, alias Chuy González, after a pursuit in Siete Ejidos, Guasave, according to Ríodoce and El País. Security Secretary García Harfuch said two men died and identification awaits genetic and fingerprint tests.
analysis.says_vs_does: Harfuch places him in the Cártel de Guasave under Fausto Isidro Meza. Outlets report he worked for both the Chapitos and the Mayiza, so his allegiance in the civil war is contested.
analysis.follow_the_money: The US offered a reward of 5 million dollars. Expansión reports that US authorities linked him in May to drug trafficking and laundering for the Sinaloa Cartel; sources do not give laundering figures.
analysis.at_stake: Mexico gains a high-value result on a US most-wanted target before federal security chiefs tour Sinaloa. His network's northern Sinaloa heroin and fentanyl production loses a senior manager.
tensions: Chapitos vs Mayiza: outlets disagree on which faction González Peñuelas served when he died.

analysis.headline: Chihuahua governor accuses Morena leader Ariadna Montiel of crime ties, and the Security Cabinet denies any intelligence report
analysis.what_happened: Chihuahua Governor Maru Campos told Carlos Loret that Morena leader Ariadna Montiel has ties to organised crime, citing a meeting involving El Guano. The federal Security Cabinet denied the meeting and any intelligence report.
analysis.says_vs_does: Both sides offer claims, not evidence. Campos has shown no documents in sources, and the federal denial came by social-media message; Montiel is preparing three legal complaints against Campos.
analysis.follow_the_money: Sources do not give a figure.
analysis.at_stake: Campos gains a national platform against Morena in a state contested by Sinaloa factions. Montiel and the federal government seek to contain a narco-politics charge against the ruling party.
tensions: Chihuahua government vs federal government: the PAN governor and Morena trade accusations, and Guanajuato's PAN governor declined to back Campos.

analysis.headline: US authorities arrest 10 alleged Sinaloa Cartel members in Florida over a Mexico-to-Tampa Bay cocaine pipeline
analysis.what_happened: US authorities arrested 10 alleged members of a Sinaloa Cartel affiliate in Florida, including cell number two Erick Manuel Gómez Tapia, alias El Canelo. CBS12 describes a cocaine pipeline from Mexico to Tampa Bay.
analysis.says_vs_does: US authorities call the cell a Sinaloa Cartel affiliate. Milenio notes that no cell name has been released and nothing ties it to the Chapitos or the Mayiza.
analysis.follow_the_money: CBS12 values the bust at 30 million dollars. Sources do not show how proceeds moved back to Mexico.
analysis.at_stake: US prosecutors show reach into cartel distribution inside the United States. The affiliate loses its Florida distribution cell.
tensions: US enforcement vs Sinaloa distribution: arrests hit the retail end of the supply chain, not its Mexican command.

analysis.headline: US sentences a Colombian Tether broker network boss and the FBI seeks an alleged Clan del Golfo launderer
analysis.what_happened: A US court sentenced Leonardo de Jesús Zuluaga Duque, alias Rey, to 13 years, El Tiempo reports. Separately, the FBI offered a reward for Víctor Julián Duque Tobón, accused of laundering for the Clan del Golfo.
analysis.says_vs_does: The Zuluaga case rests on a conviction. The Duque Tobón case rests on US accusations and an arrest warrant; sources report no arrest.
analysis.follow_the_money: Zuluaga supervised Tether brokers and helped arrange coca-paste purchases. El Heraldo reports that Duque Tobón allegedly laundered 54 million dollars through shell companies and bank accounts; the FBI reward is 10,000 dollars.
analysis.at_stake: Stablecoin brokers give traffickers a fast channel for paying suppliers. US agencies gain cases against the financial layer rather than the armed groups.
tensions: US Treasury and courts vs crypto brokers: enforcement now reaches Tether settlement of cocaine purchases.

analysis.headline: Ecuador's army seizes a gold plant tied to Los Lobos, and a mayor is detained over a laundering network
analysis.what_happened: Ecuador's army intervened a gold processing plant in Cotopaxi allegedly tied to Los Lobos. Prosecutors detained a mayor accused of leading a laundering network linked to Los Choneros and Los Lobos. Gunmen killed lawyer Leonardo Toledo in Guayaquil.
analysis.says_vs_does: President Noboa says there are signs tying opposition figure Luisa González to organised crime. Sources show his accusation but no charge on those ties.
analysis.follow_the_money: The armed forces valued the seized infrastructure and material at 6.74 million dollars. Sources do not give a figure for the mayor's alleged network.
analysis.at_stake: Los Lobos loses gold infrastructure that diversifies revenue beyond cocaine. Noboa gains a crime narrative against the Correísta opposition.
tensions: Noboa vs Correísmo: the government links its main rivals to the gangs it has declared terrorist.

analysis.headline: Senior Bolivian police officers detained over the alleged theft of millions from a drug trafficker
analysis.what_happened: El País reports that a former intelligence chief is jailed, a captain was arrested on Tuesday, and two colonels face arrest warrants. They are investigated for allegedly stealing millions of dollars from a trafficker.
analysis.says_vs_does: Officers charged with fighting trafficking allegedly kept a trafficker's money. Sources do not say what happened to the trafficker or the funds.
analysis.follow_the_money: Flow: alleged theft of drug proceeds by police officers. El País gives the sum only as millions of dollars.
analysis.at_stake: The case exposes how far trafficking money reaches into Bolivia's police command. Prosecutors gain leverage over senior officers.
tensions: Bolivian state vs its own police: the investigation targets officers rather than traffickers.

analysis.headline: Chilean minister faces impeachment over sentence cuts for men who claimed Tren de Aragua membership
analysis.what_happened: BioBioChile reports that three Venezuelans who presented themselves as Tren de Aragua members received sentence reductions under Minister Fernando Rabat. Two were freed in September. Christian Democrats joined an opposition impeachment move.
analysis.says_vs_does: Rabat says his ministry does not assess the merits of requests. The record shows decrees he signed in July and September that freed men convicted of extorting migrant women.
analysis.follow_the_money: The band extorted migrant women in La Serena in exchange for letting them work. Sources do not give a figure.
analysis.at_stake: Rabat risks removal over a crime issue central to Chilean politics. Police meanwhile report dismantling Las Águilas, another Tren de Aragua faction, in Puente Alto.
tensions: Government vs opposition: sentence-reduction decrees become an impeachment case about Tren de Aragua.

analysis.headline: Colombia carries out a sixth bombing under De La Espriella against Iván Mordisco's dissidents
analysis.what_happened: Colombian forces bombed structures of Iván Mordisco's FARC dissidents in the southwest, the sixth bombing under President De La Espriella. El Tiempo reports military intelligence remotely accessed armed groups' drone systems.
analysis.says_vs_does: De La Espriella calls the operation important and strategic. Troops were still verifying results, and sources give no casualty count.
analysis.follow_the_money: Sources do not give a figure.
analysis.at_stake: The government signals a break with Paz Total by retaking territory by force. The Defensoría warns of recruitment and displacement risk in Nariño.
tensions: State vs armed groups: analysts tie recent attacks to the state's push to retake Paz Total territory.

arc_updates.text: Navy forces killed Chuy González Peñuelas, a Cártel de Guasave figure wanted by the US, in Guasave; outlets disagree on his faction.
A US court sentenced Colombian Tether-broker boss alias Rey to 13 years, and the FBI is seeking an alleged Clan del Golfo launderer.
The army seized a gold plant tied to Los Lobos valued at 6.74 million dollars, and a mayor was detained over a gang-linked laundering network.
Colombian forces carried out a sixth bombing under De La Espriella, against Iván Mordisco's dissidents.
